items.claim: The closing-seam warrant misstates the verb forms the bytes give at Jer.39.4, and one declared substrate signal is not observed anywhere in the unit's own span.
items.evidence: The rejected alternative grounds the 39:3|39:4 seam on verse 4 turning onto the king personally 'with his own verb of flight'. The bytes contest that: the subject at MT 39:4 is compound - Zedekiah plus וְכֹ֣ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte) - and both flight-and-exit verbs are plural, וַֽ֠יִּבְרְחוּ and וַיֵּצְא֨וּ (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte); the one singular verb in the verse is וַיֵּצֵ֖א (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte), a verb of going out toward the Arabah, not of fleeing. A verb-number claim of that kind has to stand on quoted pointed bytes, and this unit quotes no Hebrew from 39:4 at all. The seam warrant the bytes do supply - verse 4's narrative-shift onset וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte) - goes uncited. Separately, the declared signal narrative_frame.reign_change_notice is not observed in Jer.39.1-Jer.39.3: both dated frames count regnal years TO an ongoing reign, בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠תְּשִׁעִית לְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.1, byte) and בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ לְצִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.2, byte), and nothing in the span reports a change of reign. What holds and should be preserved: both date shapes verify against the classified inventory (39:1 verse-initial year-word, 39:2 verse-initial bet-prefixed cardinal), the device note's contrast of where the bet-prefix lands is byte-true, the resh-family Nebuchadnezzar spelling is named at its own site, and the SAMEKH at MT 39:1 with the SAMEKH-plus-PE pair at MT 38:28 match the mark inventory under the correct types with PE and SAMEKH kept distinct. The span carries no K/Q note and no paseq, so nothing further is owed there.

items.evidence: The K/Q inventory records one variant note at MT 39:12, which sits inside this unit's own span Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14. The verse bytes carry an unpointed written form standing without a pointed counterpart beside it, כִּ֗י אם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ (oshb:Jer.39.12, byte). The unit discloses the special-letter seg at MT 39:13 and the SAMEKH at MT 39:14, so disclosure symmetry across the span is owed and this note is not exempt; MT 39:12 appears neither in the prose nor in the evidence refs, and the verse is passed over between verse 11 and verse 13. Symmetry in these layers is a sweep across the span, not a spot cite. Second, the roster is said to name four officers. MT 39:13 names three, each carrying its own title - נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָ֣ן רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים וּנְבֽוּשַׁזְבָּן֙ רַב סָרִ֔יס וְנֵרְגַ֥ל שַׂר אֶ֖צֶר רַב מָ֑ג (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte) - followed by the collective וְכֹ֖ל רַבֵּ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte). What holds and should be preserved: the special-letter handling is exact and does not over-reach the witness - the seg is x-small, it is disclosed single-witness, and the final letter carrying its accent occurs exactly once in MT 39:13 (count: 1 in-verse), at the end of וּנְבֽוּשַׁזְבָּן֙ (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte), so attributing it to that name is byte-determinable rather than assumed; no small-letter claim is made at any other site. items.claim: The opening-seam warrant misdescribes the word-event system: the shape it contrasts Jer.39.15 against is not verb-initial, and the system carries three counted shapes rather than two.
items.evidence: The structural observation at the seam is byte-true - MT 39:15 fronts the addressee phrase ahead of the verb, וְאֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.39.15, byte) - and 39:15 belongs to none of the counted shapes, so the non-membership finding stands. The stated ground does not. The unit argues that 39:15 reads that way 'rather than opening with the verb as the book's two counted narrative shapes do', but the superscription shape is not verb-initial: it opens with the article-noun, הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte), with the verb standing third. The inventory carries three counted shapes, not two (vayehi-debar-YHWH 21 verses, hadavar-asher-hayah-el-Yirmeyahu 11 verses, asher-hayah-debar-YHWH-el-Yirmeyahu 4 verses), and of those three exactly one is verb-initial - the vayehi shape - since the second opens with the article-noun and the third with the relative particle; so naming 'the book's two counted narrative shapes' collapses the system the unit is invoking as its warrant. Two further under-engagements ride on the same seam. The declared full divine-title stack is byte-present in the span - כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.39.16, byte) - but is never quoted, tier-labelled, or mouth-named in the prose, and it is the one speech formula the unit declares. And the close is argued at Jer.39.18 without the postpositive closure token that stands at both MT 39:17 and MT 39:18 (sweep: 2 verses inside this span), first attested in the span as נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.39.17, byte). Calling the fronted element the 'object' is also loose: it is a prepositional addressee phrase, while the clause subject is the word-of-YHWH phrase itself. What holds: the K/Q at MT 39:16 is correctly disclosed as present-but-not-engaged, and the SAMEKH marks at MT 39:14 and MT 39:18 verify under the correct type with single-witness tier-3 labelling; the declared false positive on the verse-14 absence claim is confirmed - MT 39:14 carries no word-event language and the negative is checkable from that verse's own bytes.
tier_citations: parashah SAMEKH MT 39:14 and MT 39:18 (single-witness, tier-3 weak)

items.claim: The device note asserts that Gedaliah is not named in this stretch, but the name stands inside the unit's own byte-tier splice of Jer.40.5; and the paseq inside the span is undisclosed while the K/Q in the same span is disclosed.
items.evidence: The note states that Gedaliah is not yet named directly in this stretch and that the advice points at him 'by kinship alone', citing בֶן אֲחִיקָ֣ם (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte). The bytes contradict this outright: MT 40:5 reads וְשֻׁ֡בָה אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֣ה בֶן אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן שָׁפָ֡ן (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte) - the personal name גְּדַלְיָ֣ה (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte) stands immediately before that patronymic, inside the very run this unit quotes at byte tier in its own rationale, and the rendering quoted beside it names him as well. The cited splice was cut to begin after the name. The claim is therefore false in both witnesses and self-contradicted by the unit's own quoted evidence. It also passes over a name-form site: MT 40:5 is one of only four verses carrying the short spelling (sweep: 4 verses - Jer.40.5, Jer.40.6, Jer.40.8, Jer.41.16, token-bound), against the long spelling used elsewhere in the same stretch. Second, the paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:1, inside the span Jer.40.1-Jer.40.5. The unit discloses the K/Q at MT 40:3 and the SAMEKH at MT 39:18 but not this seg; one engaged apparatus item in a span owes the rest, and this layer is disclosed by sweep, not spot cite. What holds and should be preserved: the frame handling at the seam is exact. MT 40:1 carries the aleph-lamed form אֶֽל (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte) inside הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte), not the one-site ayin-lamed variant, so its membership in the eleven-verse superscription shape is byte-correct; and the unit discloses that the shape here frames a release narrative rather than sermon content instead of letting the formula misname the unit. The K/Q at MT 40:3 is stated in the right direction and matches the bytes. One declared flag needs qualification rather than confirmation: within Jer.40.1-Jer.40.5 a speaker is in fact introduced at MT 40:2 and the narration resumes inside MT 40:5, so 'no new speaker or addressee' is defensible only as a seam judgement, not as a description of the bytes.
